intro:
Birmingham is the UK's second city — 1.2 million people in the city itself, 4.3 million across the wider metropolitan area — and its search results are fought over accordingly. From Jewellery Quarter workshops to Digbeth studios to professional firms on Colmore Row, thousands of businesses are chasing the same page-one spots.

I help Birmingham businesses win those spots. Direct, senior-level SEO with no account managers and no junior handoffs: technical fixes, content that answers real searches, and backlinks from sites that actually matter. You always know exactly what was done and what it earned you.

why.heading: Why Generic SEO Fails in Birmingham
why.body:
Greater Birmingham and Solihull is home to 72,620 enterprises, and business, professional and financial services alone account for 35% of the area's economic output. That means the most valuable searches in this city — solicitors, accountants, financial advisers, commercial services — are contested by firms with serious marketing budgets.

Then there is the geography. A commuter catchment stretching across the Black Country into Wolverhampton, Walsall and Dudley widens every 'near me' search. Neighbourhood intent splits hard: someone searching in Digbeth wants something different from someone in Sutton Coldfield or Moseley. The Balti Triangle and a huge student population keep food, nightlife and lettings searches fiercely competitive all year. A generic national campaign treats all of this as one market. It is not.

section1.heading: How I Run SEO for Birmingham Businesses
section1.body:
Everything starts with a full audit: your site, your Google Business Profile, your reviews, and the competitors currently outranking you. Then we agree on the target searches — the terms that actually bring enquiries, not vanity keywords — and I work through fixes in order of impact.

For Birmingham that usually means tightening the map presence first (categories, photos, review velocity), then location and service pages built around real neighbourhood intent, then content that earns links from Birmingham publications and business sites. Every month you get a plain-English report showing what changed, what moved, and what is next. No jargon, no mystery tasks, no lock-in.

section2.heading: Content That Answers Real Birmingham Searches
section2.body:
Content that ranks in Birmingham answers the questions customers actually type. A Jewellery Quarter retailer does not need another generic 'engagement rings' page — it needs the page that answers 'where to get a ring resized in Birmingham' or 'custom wedding rings Jewellery Quarter'. A Balti Triangle restaurant needs the page that settles 'best curry Birmingham city centre' for a visitor who has never been.

I build pages around that real intent: the problems, the comparisons, the 'near me' qualifiers — the student in Selly Oak and the buyer in Harborne alike. Each page has to earn its place by being genuinely useful. One page that truly satisfies a searcher outperforms twenty thin ones, and it keeps compounding for years.

faqs.q: How much does SEO cost in Birmingham?
faqs.a: Honest answer: it depends on your competition, but most Birmingham businesses I work with invest between £495 and £1,950 per month. A one-off technical audit runs £400–£800. Anyone quoting a fixed monthly price before auditing your market is guessing — the price should follow the audit, not precede it.

faqs.q: Should I target the Black Country as well as Birmingham?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Wolverhampton, Walsall and Dudley commuters search Birmingham terms constantly, and the catchment overlaps heavily. I build this as honest, distinct targeting — separate location pages with genuinely different content — rather than one page with three town names stuffed into it.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take in Birmingham?
faqs.a: Early movement in two to three months is typical, with meaningful change in four to six. City-centre professional services and other high-value niches take longer because competitors spend heavily; suburban and trade niches can move faster. Anyone promising page one in 30 days is selling you something.

faqs.q: My Digbeth competitors outrank me — what are they doing right?
faqs.a: In Digbeth's creative cluster the bar for content is higher than average, because your competitors are marketers and studios. They are usually winning on three things: genuinely useful content, links from Birmingham publications and industry sites, and an active review profile. The audit shows exactly which of the three is your gap.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate Google Business Profile for each Birmingham branch?
faqs.a: If each branch is staffed and serves customers at that address, yes — separate profiles let you appear in each neighbourhood's map pack. What you must not do is create profiles for virtual addresses or fake locations; Google suspends those fast. Service-area businesses get one profile set up correctly instead.
